Problem it solves: Instant itinerary planning and conversational query resolution
Input: User chat prompts, session search filters, past booking history, and real-time inventory database
Why this model type: Enables flexible multi-turn conversational reasoning over unstructured data
Success metric: Task completion rate >= 75%; † completion = user reaches a booking page or gets a direct answer without asking for a human agent; rolling 7 days; excluding chats abandoned after the first message; minimum 5,000 chats
Cost of a wrong answer: Hallucinated pricing leading to booking failure

Problem it solves: Helping high-credit users discover relevant rewards
Why this model type: Efficiently scores and ranks a large catalog with low latency
Success metric: Click-through rate >= 8%; † rolling 4 weeks; excluding staff accounts and out-of-stock items; minimum 50,000 users who saw the Store
Cost of a wrong answer: Wasting user coins on irrelevant items

Problem it solves: Answering questions and generating content in chat
Why this model type: Handles open-ended natural language understanding and multi-modal generation
Output: Natural language text or generated image
Success metric: Response relevance >= 85%; † judged by trained raters on a weekly sample; per top language; excluding requests correctly blocked for safety; minimum 1,000 rated answers per language
Cost of a wrong answer: Inappropriate or inaccurate responses damaging trust

Problem it solves: Answering detailed product queries and comparing specs
Why this model type: Combines RAG with tool calling to pull specs and execute actions
Output: Synthesized comparison text and recommendation carousels
How it learns: User clicks; † purchases of the recommended product, and later returns as the correction signal
Success metric: Conversion; † % of Rufus sessions leading to an order within 24 h, higher than matched shoppers without Rufus in an A/B test; rolling 4 weeks; excluding greeting-only sessions; minimum 100,000 sessions per group
Guardrail metric: † Return rate of Rufus-recommended orders not higher than non-Rufus orders; spec claims that contradict the product page at or below 1% in a weekly audit
Cost of a wrong answer: † Wrong spec (e.g. "waterproof") leads to a wrong purchase: two-way shipping cost, refund, lost trust, possible misleading-claims complaints. If Rufus adds to cart or buys: an unwanted order and an angry customer

Problem it solves: Delivering quick, personalized daily news summaries
Why this model type: Optimizes content sequencing without heavy LLM overhead
Success metric: Session retention D7 >= 40%; † rolling 4 weeks; excluding first-day users with no history; minimum 50,000 new users per cohort
Cost of a wrong answer: † Users miss important news or see only one topic (filter bubble); chasing clicks drifts the feed toward sensational stories, hurting trust and advertiser safety; a false story ranked high brings legal and regulatory heat
